A qualified total height paired with the diameter of the same tree is required.
Dominant height and a stand inventory with its density and area are required.
H and D refer to the same tree. The origin of the height must be known. Stand Hdom/Dg is a separate indicator; no automatic stability threshold is applied.
S % requires N/ha, dominant height of the same population, effectively surveyed area and an explicit square or equilateral triangular convention. Marked stems alone are insufficient.
Quality comes from recorded assessments, whose grading reference needs to be checked.
Assortments, cut specifications and prices require their own references. Quality alone does not determine timber value.

Data to complete: soil, water, site context and climate references.
These observations alone cannot predict development or diagnose the site. Find linked assessments in Explore.
H/D pairs the diameter and total height of the same tree. The height origin — measured or estimated — and its method must be known.
S % describes an inventoried stand: dominant height, density, population and effectively surveyed area must match. Stand Hdom/Dg differs from individual H/D.
A merchantable or diameter-class height does not automatically qualify H/D. This help describes the required information and does not change your survey.

Diameter of a tree whose cross-sectional area equals the mean cross-sectional area of trees with usable diameters.
Dg = √(Σ D² / n) · D and Dg in cm, n usable diameters.
